title: Can a second, wall-coating particle species stop Particle Lenia rings from fusing, so that their figure-8 fissions build lineages instead of a fission-fusion foam?
summary: Particle Lenia rings from noise pinch in two by figure-8 fission and budding, but merges (100-224 per run) match or exceed splits, so the genealogy is reticulate (20261025T1500-c13-plenia-turnover-division); noise, sigma_G and mu_G changes in small boxes reduce both splits and merges (c13 screen, unpublished numbers: noise 0.01-0.03 gives 0-2 splits and 1-2 merges). Mordvintsev et al. call per-particle parameters a trivial extension. A second species B that is attracted to the ring wall's U level but repels other B particles at range ~2 would coat each ring with a repulsive shell, as amphiphile heads do; rings should then touch less and fuse less while fission (driven inside the wall) is unaffected.
experiment: Fork collective/contrib/20261025T1500-c13-plenia-turnover-division/world.py (feed=decay=0) with a species label: A as now; B (10-20% of particles) feels G at a lower mu_G so it sits on the wall's outer flank, and B-B pairs get an extra repulsion c_BB max(1 - r/2, 0)^2. Run 3500 particles in 60x60 to t=1500 on 2 seeds per arm (B fraction 0, 0.1, 0.2), and count persistent splits, clean splits, merges and merge-aware generations with splits_feed.py from that contribution. Success: merges below 50% of splits with generation >= 3. About 60-80 minutes.
